# Real 802.11 beacons and probe responses, for tests/beacon.rs.
#
# Produced by tools/beacons/extract.py from a monitor-mode capture:
#
#   sudo tcpdump -I -i en0 -w /tmp/beacons.pcap -c 2000 'type mgt'
#   tools/beacons/extract.py /tmp/beacons.pcap >> \
#       crates/wartui-proto/tests/beacon_vectors.txt
#
# Format: <name> <length> <hex>, matching golden_vectors.txt. Lines starting
# with # are ignored, so a capture can be appended unedited.
#
# The assembled frames in tests/beacon.rs check the classification ladder
# against a reading of the auth-mode rules. These check it against the air,
# which is a different question and the one that has caught things before.
#
# SCRUBBED, and the extractor does it by default. A capture of the air around
# you is a geolocation fingerprint — BSSIDs are precisely what WiGLE and the
# phone vendors run their location databases on, which is the whole premise of
# this project, and SSIDs carry surnames and house numbers. Addresses here are
# synthetic and locally administered, SSIDs are `ap-NNN` padded to the length
# the real one had, and every element the parser does not read has had its
# contents replaced — including WPS, which carries device names and serials.
#
# What survives is what is under test: every element's tag and length at its
# original offset, and the real contents of the SSID length, DS Parameter Set,
# RSN, HT Operation and WPA elements. These 91 access points cover [OPEN],
# [WPA2], [WPA2_PSK], [WPA3_PSK] and [WPA2_WPA3_PSK], and twenty of them are
# hidden.
